_comment: Launch parameters in three layers. 'policy' does not depend on the model or the platform: how the server is driven. 'profiles' is the platform layer, keyed by os+backend, and it owns what belongs to the machine — how many layers go on the GPU, and the context window and the generation budget, because those are the two values that follow the memory the machine has. 'fallback' is used only when no layer above it names a parameter (a hand-picked GGUF, a model the catalog does not know) — llama.cpp's own 4096-token default would otherwise truncate a page carrying a table. Model parameters (image-*-tokens, dry-sequence-breaker, special) live in models/<id>.json: what the weights need, which the machine cannot decide. See docs/10-model-profiles.md.

parameters.name: ctx-size
parameters.description: Model context window in tokens. Last resort for a model outside the catalog.

parameters.name: n-predict
parameters.description: Maximum tokens to generate per completion.

parameters.name: parallel
parameters.description: Number of concurrent server slots.

parameters.name: cache-reuse
parameters.description: Context reuse window between requests; 0 disables.

parameters.name: no-context-shift
parameters.description: Keep the context stable: do not shift the KV cache when the window overflows.

parameters.name: no-warmup
parameters.description: Skip the warmup run at model load (faster start, slower first request).

parameters.name: n-gpu-layers
parameters.description: Number of model layers offloaded to the GPU; 99 = all.

parameters.name: flash-attn
parameters.description: Flash attention: on, off or auto.
